prompt:
Warm editorial ink-and-wash illustration on a warm cream ground: a loose confident ink line with soft transparent washes over it, muted earth palette of cream, rust, ochre, mustard, sage and warm grey, quiet and hand-made, the register of a good picture book rather than a comic.

Character reference: PIP, a SMALL HAND-MADE TIN-TOY ROBOT, cute and endearing, standing alone on a plain empty cream background. Shown FULL BODY head to feet, front three-quarter view.

He is SMALL, only about KNEE-HIGH TO A CHILD, and reads unmistakably as a little tin toy rather than a machine. A ROUND TIN HEAD that is SLIGHTLY TOO BIG for his body, which is what makes him endearing. TWO ROUND DARK GLASS EYES, simple and wide-set, each with a single warm highlight. A SMALL ROUND BRASS GRILLE below the eyes that he speaks through. ONE SMALL AMBER PILOT BULB on top of his head, warm and dim, which does NOT glow and does NOT cast light on anything. A BOXY DENTED TIN TORSO with one small hinged panel and visible rivets. TWO STUBBY JOINTED BRASS ARMS ending in simple THREE-FINGER HANDS. TWO SHORT STUBBY LEGS with round flat feet.

He is plainly ASSEMBLED FROM SCRAP BY CHILDREN: dented, scratched and patinated, mismatched panels of tin in slightly different tones, one arm a different metal from the other, solder visible at the seams. He is NEVER sleek and NEVER new.

His whole bearing is EAGER AND WILLING: leaning slightly forward, head tilted a little, both hands up and open at chest height, plainly keen to help. He is TRYING. He is warm and lovable in the way a well-loved old tin toy is lovable.

ABSOLUTELY NOT, these are the rejected poles of this style and any of them is a failure: neon, 3D or CGI or Pixar rendering, glossy plastic, chrome, sleek modern product design, HUD or arc-reactor comic vocabulary, neo-comic styling, photorealism, airbrushing, lens flare, heavy drop shadows, glowing screens, holograms, blue light.

Render ONE single image only. This is NOT a contact sheet, NOT a grid, NOT a multi-panel study sheet, NOT a turnaround strip. No panel borders, no captions, no labels, no annotation text of any kind.

DEVICE ANATOMY, NON-NEGOTIABLE: any phone, laptop, tablet or monitor is anatomically correct. The GLOWING DISPLAY is on the SCREEN side, and that side FACES ITS USER. A person looking at a device sees its screen; the viewer therefore sees the device's BACK or EDGE plus the light it throws onto the user's face and hands. NEVER put the screen image on the back of a phone, on a laptop's outer lid, or on a monitor's rear. NEVER show a screen facing the camera while the person using it looks at the opposite side. If both the user's face and the screen content must be visible, shoot it over the user's shoulder.

READABLE SURFACES FACE THEIR READER: any book, page, letter, scroll or sign a character is reading or writing faces THAT CHARACTER, never the camera. Compose over-the-shoulder or from behind so the surface genuinely faces them. Any handwriting is abstract handwriting-like line work with NO real readable letters.

NO USER INTERFACE ANYWHERE: no windows, menu bars, buttons, icons, toolbars, panels, form fields, cursors, floating rectangles or screenshot-like elements. Screens carry only soft glow or vague painterly shapes.
